faq.q: ### How are gains from debt mutual funds taxed after April 2023?
faq.a: For investments made on or after April 1, 2023, all gains from debt mutual funds are treated as short-term capital gains and added to your total income, taxed at your applicable income tax slab rate.

faq.q: ### What is the main advantage of EPF over debt mutual funds for retirement?
faq.a: EPF offers guaranteed returns and capital safety, backed by the government. For contributions up to ₹2.5 lakhs annually, the interest earned is entirely tax-free.

faq.q: ### Are debt mutual funds still a good investment for high-income earners?
faq.a: They can still be considered for diversification and liquidity, but their tax efficiency has significantly reduced post-April 2023, as all gains are now taxed at your income slab rate.

faq.q: ### Can I withdraw from EPF before retirement?
faq.a: Partial withdrawals are allowed for specific circumstances like housing, education, or medical emergencies, subject to certain conditions and service periods. Full withdrawal is typically at retirement or extended unemployment.

faq.q: ### What is VPF and how is it taxed?
faq.a: VPF (Voluntary Provident Fund) allows employees to contribute more than the mandatory 12% to their PF account. Its taxation is the same as EPF; interest on combined employee contributions (mandatory + VPF) exceeding ₹2.5 lakhs annually is taxable.

faq.q: ### Should I stop my VPF contributions if I'm in the 30% tax bracket?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If your total employee contribution (mandatory + VPF) is below ₹2.5 lakhs, VPF remains highly tax-efficient. If it exceeds this, you should compare its post-tax returns with other options like debt funds or NPS.
